final_answer:
The receptor-subtype genomic landscapes differed strongly in the supplied MSK-IMPACT cohort after excluding unknown/equivocal receptor calls (n=1,814): HR+HER2- n=1,362, HR+HER2+ n=132, HR-HER2+ n=70, TNBC n=250.

HR+HER2- tumors were PI3K/luminal dominated: PIK3CA mutation 42.5%, GATA3 18.0%, CDH1 18.1%, MAP3K1 9.8%, ESR1 10.3%, and AKT1 6.4%, with comparatively low TP53 mutation (23.2%). Enrichment tests supported PIK3CA, GATA3, ESR1, CDH1, MAP3K1 and AKT1 enrichment and TP53/RB1/NF1 depletion versus other subtypes.

HER2-positive tumors were defined by ERBB2 amplification: 79.5% in HR+HER2+ and 90.0% in HR-HER2+. HR+HER2+ combined ERBB2 amplification with TP53 mutation 47.0% and PIK3CA mutation 31.8%. HR-HER2+ was more TP53-high (78.6%) while retaining PIK3CA mutation 32.9%.

TNBC was TP53/RB1/PTEN-loss enriched: TP53 mutation 81.2%, RB1 mutation 11.2%, RB1 deep deletion 5.6%, PTEN deep deletion 4.4%, and the highest median TMB (0.167 mutations/Mb). TNBC was depleted for PIK3CA, GATA3, ESR1, CDH1, ERBB2 amplification, and CCND1/FGF amplifications, while showing higher MYC amplification (15.6%) and enriched KDM5A/ETV6 amplification signals.

Overall, HR+ disease—especially HR+HER2-—was luminal/PI3K-pathway enriched, HER2-positive disease was ERBB2-amplicon driven, and TNBC was dominated by TP53 alteration with RB1/PTEN loss and higher TMB. Full trace, code, intermediate counts, statistical tests, limitations, and output table paths are in trace.md.
